      Creative work

      Three pieces of work this year that went past the brief, plus the steady output that runs underneath all of it.

      HIGHLIGHT 01

      Service Awards toolkit

      Rolled out across Europe

      Every market was announcing its awards differently. We built one design system for the whole of Europe, so that when a subsidiary wins something, the work is already done.

      Each award comes with a ready asset pack built to the new Samsung brand guidelines: support banners, social posts, stories, email modules and video end frames. Drop in the award name and publish.

      • One visual language for every European market
      • Built to the latest Samsung brand guidelines
      • Covers support pages, social, email and video
      • Template based, so a market needs no design resource
      • Award name and year are the only variables

      The full pack: support banners, social formats, stories, print and video end frames, all from one system.

      The pack includes a motion end frame so the award shows up in video as well as on the page. Same system, same build, no extra brief.

      Block 02 · Going beyond

      Best practices

      Five things any market can copy, and one rule set everyone now has to follow.

      PRACTICE 01

      Learn from the language neighbours

      Somebody has usually answered the question already, in a market that shares your language. For SEAS, that is Germany. For SEBN, that is France.

      Start in Community: the most commented threads tell you what people are actually stuck on. Then check whether we already hold that content. If we do not, copy it. If it does not fit, adapt it. Widen the search to other markets when the answer is not there.

      • SEAS looks to Germany, SEBN looks to France
      • Start with the most commented Community topics
      • Check for duplicates before building anything
      • Copy where it fits, adapt where it does not
      • Look wider when neither market has it

      PRACTICE 02

      Cross-border coordination: monthly alignment calls

      Monthly alignment calls with SEAS and SEBN to strengthen collaboration, exchange insights across markets and identify opportunities for improvement.

      These sessions keep us aligned, let each market draw inspiration from what has already worked elsewhere, and set clear priorities for the month ahead.

      • Define key focus areas and actions for the current month
      • Review upcoming requests and identify new opportunities
      • Explore ideas and inspiration from other markets
      • Share best practices and high-performing content across markets
      • Align on priorities and ongoing activities

      PRACTICE 03

      Keep Jira as the one channel

      Every request through the ticket, every time. A request raised in an email, a chat or on a call is a request nobody can see, prioritise or measure.

      It is also the only way the turnaround numbers in block one mean anything.

      • One channel, one queue, one history
      • Nothing gets lost between people
      • Status is visible to the market at any moment
      • Everything is measurable, so everything is improvable

      PRACTICE 04

      Open new channels with the content you already have

      A published FAQ is not finished. It is the source for a Community post, and the Community post is a second route into the same answer.

      Link them to each other, and the traffic and the insights compound instead of sitting in one page.

      • FAQ published, then a Community post built from it
      • Cross-link both ways, so each sends traffic to the other
      • Reuse rather than rewrite
      • Community comments become the next content brief

      PRACTICE 05

      Close the content gaps between your own markets

      Inside one entity the sites should hold the same answers. If Austria has 50 pages on a topic, Switzerland should have 50.

      Site coverage in block one is exactly this gap, measured.

      • Compare page counts site by site, not entity by entity
      • Where one site is short, the content usually already exists
      • Levelling up is adaptation, not production
      • Watch it in the HCR coverage figures

      PRACTICE 06

      The new AI content rules

      Samsung’s AI Content Playbook now governs anything AI touches, visual and written. The visual rules are not negotiable; the writing rules are how a page gets found and cited.

      • No AI humans. No photorealistic people. Film them, or limit AI to hands and arms in product shots
      • No AI product. Never generate the product, the lettermark or the UI. Official assets only
      • Disclose and clear. Platform AI labels, local disclosure law, no third-party IP, legal review before launch
      • Human in the loop. Review at every stage, not just at the end
      • Approved tools only, every asset logged, all AI content submitted to SBVI

      HOW WE WRITE IT

      Written for people first, then for the machines reading it

      Never

      • Duplicate content across pages or markets
      • A page written entirely by AI

      Always

      • The title is a question
      • The first paragraph answers it in about 70 words
      • Question and answer structure throughout
      • Bullets rather than paragraphs
      • Tables and concrete data wherever possible

      Block 02 · Going beyond

      New tools

      Three platforms now in the production line, each aimed at a specific line in the cost, quality and visibility numbers.

      TOOL 01

      Profound

      In use now

      AI search intelligence and brand visibility. A platform that monitors and analyses how Samsung and its products appear across AI-powered search engines, including ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini.

      It tells us where brand visibility stands, tracks how products are recommended, shows what competitors are doing, and finds the gaps where Samsung’s position in AI-driven search can be strengthened.

      • Monitors ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and AI Overviews
      • Tracks citation share for samsung.com against every other domain
      • Measures sentiment across support and service themes
      • Shows competitor visibility side by side
      • Every AI figure in this review came from it

      The AI visibility and citation data behind block one comes from this platform.

      TOOL 02

      Adobe Firefly

      Approved for commercial use

      AI-powered creative asset generation. Our approved AI tool for generating and adapting visual assets. Firefly sits inside the creative production workflow, so we can create new imagery, modify existing assets and explore visual concepts faster.

      Fully aligned with Samsung’s latest AI guidelines, which is the part that matters: assets generated with it meet the standard required for commercial use.

      • Approved under Samsung’s current AI guidelines
      • Generates new imagery and adapts existing assets
      • Used to explore concepts before committing production time
      • Cleared for commercial use, not just internal mockups
      • Sits alongside illustration and motion, it does not replace them

      TOOL 03

      Automated post-live QA with Playwright

      In use now

      Playwright is an open-source automation framework for web testing. At CPC we built a Playwright script that automatically compares published pages against the approved master documents stored in GitHub.

      It finds content discrepancies after a page goes live, cuts the manual effort out of checking, and keeps published content accurate without anyone reading the same page twice.

      Best use case: high-volume banner QA. 50 pages validated in 7 minutes.

      • Automated post-live validation of published pages
      • Compares live URLs against master documents in GitHub
      • Identifies discrepancies between approved and published content
      • Cuts manual QA effort while improving accuracy and consistency
      • 50 pages in 7 minutes on banner QA

      Block 03 · Concept

      Conversational chatbot

      A support assistant with the whole content library behind it, answering in its own words rather than returning a pre-written reply.

      THE IDEA

      Not a decision tree

      The chatbots a customer meets today follow a script. You pick from a menu, the menu narrows, and if your problem is not on the menu you end up at a contact form.

      This one reads the question as written, searches everything we have published, and composes an answer. If the answer is not in the library, it says so rather than guessing.

      • Understands the question as the customer phrased it
      • Answers from the full library, not a scripted branch
      • Cites the page the answer came from
      • Says when it does not know, instead of inventing
      • Works in every language the library is published in

      WHY IT RAISES THE VALUE OF CONTENT

      It is only as good as what is underneath

      A conversational assistant does not replace the pages. It reads them. Every weakness in the library becomes a weakness in the answer, and every gap becomes a question it cannot answer.

      Which is exactly why the writing rules in block two matter: a page structured as a question with a short direct answer is a page a model can use.

      • Coverage gaps become unanswered questions
      • Out of date pages become wrong answers
      • Duplicate pages become inconsistent answers
      • Clean structure and real data make it work better
      ← Back to What's next

      Block 03 · Concept

      Proofreading agent

      An automated pass before a page reaches QA: the small things that are easy to miss and slow to check by hand.

      THE IDEA

      Catch it before a person has to

      Most of what QA finds is mechanical: a bold that was never applied, a link that goes nowhere, a heading at the wrong level, a model name that does not exist in this market, a missing legal line.

      None of that needs a human to find. It needs a human to decide what to do about it.

      • Formatting: missing bold, inconsistent headings, broken list structure
      • Links: dead links, wrong destinations, missing anchors
      • Accuracy: model names, variants, specs, legal lines per market
      • Terminology against the market glossary
      • Structure against the AI content guidelines
      • Flags, never rewrites and never publishes
      Pre-QA check
      ✓ Terminology matches market glossary
      ✓ Model names and variants verified
      ✓ Title is a question, answered in the opening paragraph
      ! Step 3 instruction not bolded
      ! 2 links return 404
      ! Legal line missing for this market

      An illustration of the output, not a live tool.

      WHERE IT HITS

      The step it takes out

      QA sits in the production stage of every request. The repetitive part of it is the part this removes, which is also the part that gets slower as volume rises.

      • Cuts the rework loop between production and QA
      • Keeps the AI content rules enforced on every page, not just the reviewed ones
      • Scales with volume instead of against it
      • Frees QA hours for judgement rather than checking
